commenti.body:
I’m Brazilian and here this movie is considered a true timeless classic and often people feel like it not having the Oscar was highly unfair due to Harvey Weinstein influence. 

Anyway, personally I do not care that much about the Oscars. 

I’ve watched this film long ago when I was around 16 or something and all I remember is that this movie is so sad that I’ve never watched it again.

Always appreciated that movie for its swift plot, its incredible acting, and lovely cinematography. As a city-raised Brazilian, it hits some nice "aint the country folk charming" notes, although these days it might hit differently, as a little condescending.

  
Regardless, it's definitely one of the better old-person-stuck-with-kid-who-changes-their-perspective-on-life movies, Walter Salles is a pretty gifted director, and, yes, emotionally, it's got a lot of gut punches, so prepare yourself to see gut-wrenching cruelty, tear-inducing heartbreak, and quite a bit of bittersweet joy. Oh man, crying about it now, and it's been a good 15 years since I've seen it.
I am from Serbia and I cried when I watched it. It's a wonderfully told story.
It doesn't get talked about enough I think, really good and sad movie
Well that happens with a loooot of good movies (mainly foreing ones).

Me and my dad love this film.

It has gotten a bit of critical pushback in the last ten years or so, as it sort of represents a tendency of showing brazilian poor/countryside people as having some sort of inherent gracefulness that sanitizes the harsh real conditions in favor of disconnected humanism. Walter Salles's films as well as his brother's (João Moreira Salles, whose films I actually really dislike) are accused of this frequently, as they're both from an extremely wealthy family composed of bank owners, ambassadors, etc.

In whatever way one could criticize those aspects as they're worked through in the film, it overall does a good job. The actors are all fantastic and so well directed, they make all the different surrounding ambients so full of life. It feels a lot like a "classic" film in the way the two main characters are chosen to tell the story, reminds me a lot of Anna Magnani films, in a way.
yes, that was such an amazing movie, and it really pissed me off that they gave the Oscar to Gwyneth Paltrow for Shakespeare and love instead of the actress who starred in this Brazilian masterpiece
